proposal.title: Aurelia vendor variants — display input
proposal.reason: Apply the author's vendor-owned/vendor-sold cooperation model and inclusive midpoint >=70% rule. Probabilities are subjective scenario judgments, not historical observations or shipment guarantees. Logix provides design help and AION may supply chips; no OEM-only supply to Logix, Logix ownership or Logix resale is assumed. Preserve historical records and add linked, separately dated scenario offerings. Sanyo VM-4209 — Logix digital-input variant: 65–80%, midpoint 72.5%, estimated release 1980-05. Leedex Video 100 — Logix digital-input variant: 75–90%, midpoint 82.5%, estimated release 1980-03. Netronics keyboard — FlexiBUS/TUI variant: 70–85%, midpoint 77.5%, estimated release 1980-03. Full reassessment and release basis: data_storytelling/review_evidence/aurelia-vendor-variants/assessment.json and offerings.json.

specification.description: Alternative-history Aurelia offering derived from {source_1}. {vendor} owns, manufactures, brands, sells and supports the finished product. Logix may assist with design and AION Labs may supply necessary chips and ROMs; neither becomes the finished-product owner or seller. The direct release date is an estimated scenario month, not a historical release claim. Existing source products keep their original identities and interfaces.

Sanyo manufactures and sells a branded nine-inch monitor variant with an AION-supplied digital-link receiver and video conversion electronics. Retain a composite input where the vendor design allows. Only tested raster/readability profiles are advertised; this launch assumes a qualified 40-column Aurelia profile, not automatic 80-column readability.

The vendor implements the Logix digital-video data, clock, synchronization and control interface using a receiver and conversion electronics. The monitor reports only supported profiles; host and monitor capabilities are intersected before mode selection. No passive cable conversion is sufficient. The initial variant does not imply later palette, professional-resolution or color support. Compatibility is with suitable Aurelia digital-video output, not a FlexiBUS display class.

impacted_standards.assumption_description: Alternative-history assessment at the estimated release month of this vendor-owned and vendor-sold Aurelia offering. The scenario assumes the described implementation and host integration are delivered; the date is not historical shipment evidence.
impacted_standards.comparison_description: The vendor-owned monitor implements the digital link and a qualified monochrome profile while retaining its own display construction.
impacted_standards.outcomes_description: Adds an independently sold monitor choice and expands the digital-video ecosystem while competing with Logix monitor offerings.

impacted_products.assumption_description: Alternative-history assessment at the estimated release month of this vendor-owned and vendor-sold Aurelia offering. The scenario assumes the described implementation and host integration are delivered; the date is not historical shipment evidence.
impacted_products.comparison_description: The vendor supplies the stated peripheral and compatible host integration for the Aurelia platform, including its monochrome configuration. Any narrower display mode or software requirement is stated in the specification.
impacted_products.outcomes_description: Expands what an Aurelia owner can purchase from an independent supplier; vendor ownership and sales remain separate from Logix.

specification.description: Alternative-history Aurelia offering derived from {source_1}. {vendor} owns, manufactures, brands, sells and supports the finished product. Logix may assist with design and AION Labs may supply necessary chips and ROMs; neither becomes the finished-product owner or seller. The direct release date is an estimated scenario month, not a historical release claim. Existing source products keep their original identities and interfaces.

Netronics sells a revised keyboard with a controller that reads the key matrix before ASCII encoding. It preserves key identity and modifiers, and provides arrows, Home/End, Page Up/Down, separate Backspace/Delete, Ctrl/Shift/Alt, function keys and Break. This is a new keyboard variant, not an adapter that reconstructs missing modifier events from old ASCII bytes.

The vendor implements FlexiBUS discovery, differential serial transport, framing, bounded requests/retries and flow control using Logix design assistance and AION-supplied interface components where needed. One device connects to each host port; this product supplies no implicit hub or daisy chain. Attach only while the port is quiescent. The peripheral has its own power supply unless the qualified keyboard power budget applies. Vendor-supplied Aurelia Z80/CP/M software handles this device; no arbitrary firmware auto-execution, cross-CPU binary compatibility or later networking/pointer support is implied.

Keyboard reports preserve key identity and Ctrl/Shift/Alt state separately from text translation. The revised layout and firmware satisfy the TUI keyboard-input requirements, including ambiguous byte combinations that the original ASCII keyboard cannot distinguish. Qualification covers the new hardware; it does not retroactively certify old keyboards.

specification.description: Alternative-history Aurelia offering derived from {source_1}. {vendor} owns, manufactures, brands, sells and supports the finished product. Logix may assist with design and AION Labs may supply necessary chips and ROMs; neither becomes the finished-product owner or seller. The direct release date is an estimated scenario month, not a historical release claim. Existing source products keep their original identities and interfaces.

Netronics sells a revised keyboard with a controller that reads the key matrix before ASCII encoding. It preserves key identity and modifiers, and provides arrows, Home/End, Page Up/Down, separate Backspace/Delete, Ctrl/Shift/Alt, function keys and Break. This is a new keyboard variant, not an adapter that reconstructs missing modifier events from old ASCII bytes.

The vendor implements FlexiBUS discovery, differential serial transport, framing, bounded requests/retries and flow control using Logix design assistance and AION-supplied interface components where needed. One device connects to each host port; this product supplies no implicit hub or daisy chain. Attach only while the port is quiescent. The peripheral has its own power supply unless the qualified keyboard power budget applies. Vendor-supplied Aurelia Z80/CP/M software handles this device; no arbitrary firmware auto-execution, cross-CPU binary compatibility or later networking/pointer support is implied.

Keyboard reports preserve key identity and Ctrl/Shift/Alt state separately from text translation. The revised layout and firmware satisfy the TUI keyboard-input requirements, including ambiguous byte combinations that the original ASCII keyboard cannot distinguish. Qualification covers the new hardware; it does not retroactively certify old keyboards.
